findings.text: the promoted-history feed keeps only rows whose gate equals _PROMOTED_GATE "passed" (:56), but every row ledger.picker_runs returns is a completed promotion and the declared gate vocabulary is passed/failed/not-run (reckon/ledger.py:92); the reckon ledger carries 212 implement/test rows with gate "not-run" and 146 with "failed", so a section whose node such a row delivered still reads ready and can be dispatched again, which is the duplicate this section exists to prevent, and the unlanded-run finding at reckon/roadmap.py:1948 sees the same narrowed set

a node that appears in a released-phase pointer is added to free and is not removed when the same node is later matched by a promoted row, while held_section_blockers skips any section with any free node (:223); a delivered node that was re-requested by a run that then failed, which is what the pre-fix duplicate dispatch produced, therefore leaves its section listed ready despite the promoted row holding it
section_nodes has no caller anywhere in reckon/ or tests/, and the evidence record cites it as a delivered site, so it is dead public surface rather than part of the hold

_promoted_rows hand-rolls a module-level memo keyed on a (mtime_ns, size) pair and hands callers the cached list itself, duplicating reckon/file_memo.py, which the repository declares as its one stat-identity memo, and the ledger's own indexed read at reckon/ledger.py:2222, while dropping file_memo's returned-copy protection
